2607.03228.title: Organizational Memory for Agentic Business Process Execution
2607.03228.paper_summary: LLM-based agents offer new opportunities for automating business process execution beyond the limits of rule-based systems. However, general-purpose LLMs lack the organization-specific knowledge required for reliable execution, which is typically fragmented across human-oriented artifacts such as policies, process models, and standard operating procedures. While such knowledge can technically be encoded in individual prompts or agent-specific retrieval setups, this approach does not scale in enterprises, as it gives rise to knowledge silos and rule duplicates, and makes consistent updates and learning across agents difficult. We argue that this calls for an organizational memory for agentic business process execution: a shared, governed, and agent-consumable reference layer of evolving organization-specific procedural knowledge about how work should be executed. We derive requirements for such a memory, propose an architecture for its curation and consumption, and demonstrate its effectiveness in a proof-of-concept based on a procurement scenario.
2607.03228.paper_summary_zh: LLM 基礎的代理提供了自動化業務流程執行的新機會，超越了基於規則系統的限制。<lb/>然而，通用 LLM 缺乏可靠執行所需的組織特定知識，這些知識通常分散在以人為導向的文檔中，例如政策、流程模型和標準作業程序。<lb/>雖然這些知識在技術上可以編碼在單個提示或代理特定的檢索設置中，但這種方法在企業中無法擴展，因為它會導致知識孤島和規則重複，並使得在代理之間進行一致的更新和學習變得困難。<lb/>我們認為這需要一個組織記憶，以便進行代理業務流程執行：一個共享的、受管理的和代理可消耗的參考層，包含有關工作應如何執行的持續演變的組織特定程序知識。<lb/>我們推導出這種記憶的需求，提出其策劃和消耗的架構，並在基於採購場景的概念驗證中展示其有效性。
